text:
Maya: Hey team :wave: I'm planning to relocate my home base to Mexico City for ~18 months starting July. Quick q on what happens to WFH stipend / benefits / payroll tax stuff. Don’t need a full deep dive yet, just high-level next steps.
Jordan (People Ops): Congrats, Maya! :tada: Short version — we'll need the relocation form + confirmation of dates. Payroll may need to switch you to local payroll or set up cross-border payroll. WFH stipend is pro-rated based on change date.
Maya: Cool. Do I need to give 30 days notice to change home base? Any visa stuff I should flag? I’m a US-based employee with an expat permit.
Jordan (People Ops): For long-term moves (>90 days) we treat it as a home-base change. 30 days notice is preferred but not mandatory — gives us time to check tax nexus. If you're keeping US benefits, we need to check local eligibility in MX. If you need a work visa there, that’s on you but we’ll support documentation.
Carlos (Payroll): FYI payroll implications: Depending on state/local regs, we may keep you on US payroll for up to X months via remote work policy, but 18 months likely triggers local payroll or registered employer in MX. That can affect withholding, social contributions, and employer-side taxes.
Maya: Ugh, so could the company ask me to switch to MX payroll and lose some US benefits?
Anna (Benefits): We try to maintain core coverage where possible. Some plans (US-only) can’t be extended abroad. If MX payroll is required, enrollment options may change — we’ll map out equivalencies for medical, dental, and retirement. We’ll also explain any changes to employee premiums.
Jordan (People Ops): Practical next steps for you, Maya: paste this checklist into your calendar and ping us when step 1 is done.
people-ops-bot: ```
1) Fill relocation form: https://intranet.redwood.com/relocate-form
2) Add planned move dates + address
3) Submit proof of local residency/permit when available
4) People Ops runs tax nexus + payroll recommendation (3-7 business days)
5) If MX payroll required, Payroll will send onboarding docs
6) Benefits team maps coverage changes
```
Maya: Thanks — timeline question: how long does payroll vendor setup take if MX payroll is needed?
Carlos (Payroll): Vendor onboarding typically 2-4 weeks once we approve the country. If we need local registration (entity/branch), that can be months and is handled at enterprise level — but for 18 months we usually use local payroll vendor (Papaya/Remote/LocalPTO vendor). We’ll give a final recommendation after the nexus check.
Maya: And WFH stipend? Do I lose it if I'm abroad?
Jordan (People Ops): WFH stipend policies: prorated for partial months, continued for most long-term remote cases unless local law or payroll prevents us from paying an allowance. If you move to MX payroll, stipend will be processed through payroll and may be taxable locally.
Anna (Benefits): Also note: if you enroll in local health plan, some HSA/FSA options from US plans may not apply. We’ll run your specific scenario and share net-pay examples.
Maya: Ok great. Can you confirm who I should loop in for immigration docs if needed?
Jordan (People Ops): Loop in me + people-ops-ops@redwood.com. If you need company letters for visa, we’ll generate them after the form. For any legal questions about local employment law, we’ll escalate to legal.
Carlos (Payroll): One more: if MX creates a tax nexus, it could affect headcount reporting for that country. This is standard but we’ll flag any material exposures.
Maya: Thanks all — I’ll fill the relocation form this afternoon. Will post the dates here once submitted. :thumbsup:
Jordan (People Ops): Perfect. Tag me and I’ll kick off the nexus check. :sparkles:
